issues.description: Transform is silently skipped when splitting via delimiter on a single string
issues.detail: When delimiter splits a single string into items, the subsequent code path differs from the multi-value branch. The reader cannot easily tell whether the user-supplied transform is applied to each split element. State the invariant explicitly: 'after this block, items is a list of strings on which transform will be applied uniformly.' Add a test asserting transform runs on each split element.

issues.description: keep_blank_qs_values interaction with delimiter splitting is documented but not tested
issues.detail: The docstring claims keep_blank_qs_values has no effect on secondary splitting, yet no test verifies the behavior for inputs like 'a,,b' or 'a| |b'. Empty fragments after split are a classic off-by-one source. Add tests pinning the contract; otherwise the documented invariant is unaudited and may drift.

issues.description: Delimiter lookup table conflates symbolic constants with literal characters
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS maps both ',' to ',' and 'pipeDelimited' to '|'. The self-mapping of literals is a small notational smell; a set of allowed literals plus a small alias dict would express intent more clearly. Minor literate-programming nit, not a correctness issue.

issues.description: Error message lists supported delimiters as an unordered tuple over dict keys
issues.detail: tuple(_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS) relies on dict insertion order for a user-facing message. Stable, but a sorted tuple would be kinder to the reader and to documentation tooling. Tiny readability point.

issues.description: No test for delimiter combined with a transform callable
issues.detail: get_param_as_list accepts a transform argument, but none of the added tests exercise delimiter together with transform. Given the existing test matrix is otherwise thorough, this is a small gap worth one parametrized case to lock the contract.

review.summary: The change is small, localized, and the test matrix is respectable: comma/space/pipe, symbolic constants, percent-encoded pipe, auto_parse_qs_csv interaction, and multi-value query strings are all covered. Decision: RIGOROUS on the happy paths, UNDER-AUDITED on a few edges. The loop invariant of get_param_as_list after the new block is straightforward to state ('items is a non-empty list of strings, possibly produced by splitting a single value'), and complexity is O(n) in the value length, which is appropriate. My concerns are pinning down transform interaction and the documented keep_blank_qs_values claim with explicit tests, plus minor literate-programming nits around the lookup table and error message ordering.
